Enodia

Hades 2 Build Companion

Roadmap · August 2026

Nothing is built yet

A tool for the boon you are about to take.

Every Hades 2 build site tells you what a finished build does. None of them help you at the Exit, holding two Hera boons, staring at three offers with fifteen seconds to decide. This one is being built for that moment.

The premise

You do not choose your build up front.

Most build tools answer one question: out of everything in the game, what is best. That works when you pick your whole loadout up front from a fixed list. Hades 2 does not work that way. You pick an Exit, and the god behind it offers you three boons, holding whatever you already have, with no idea what the next Exit offers. That is a different question, and it needs a different tool.

Which builds are still live

You are not chasing one boon. You are somewhere inside several possible builds at once, and each pick moves you toward some and away from others.

What just died

Commit your Cast and a dozen builds quietly close. The game will keep showing you their requirements anyway. Nothing tells you to stop trying.

What you were doing

Quit at a boss, come back a week later, and you have forgotten what you were building. The save is fine. You are the part that lost the thread.

“I kept trying for that Zeus legendary. Turns out I needed the boon on my Cast, and I never picked it.”

A worked example

What it actually does at an Exit

These are real boons with the game's real requirements, read out of the game files. It is not a mockup with made up names.

You are running Sister Blades, ten rooms in. You are holding Heart Breaker from Aphrodite and two boons from Hera. Your Cast slot is still empty. You clear an Encounter and two Exits open. There are two decisions here, not one, and the first one matters more. Try it. Pick an Exit.

Step 1

Which Exit

You commit to a god before you see a single boon.

Step 2

Which of the three

Rerolls exist, but they cost more each time you use one.

Coverage

It knows the whole game

Every god who grants boons, every duo between them, and the exact prerequisites for each. The data is read from the game's own files rather than copied off a wiki, so a patch means re-running a script instead of re-reading someone's guide.

16Boon sources
37Duo boons
25Arcana cards
24Weapon aspects
47Hammer upgrades
5Boon slots

It also tracks where you are in the run, because the number of Exits left is part of what makes a build reachable or not.

Under the hood

Things the game never tells you

Building this means reading the game's own code, and that turns up rules nobody is told. Some of them you would never have found. Some you would have worked out eventually, and it would have been more fun to find them yourself. So they are sorted by that, and nothing opens unless you open it.

Level 1

You were never going to work this out

Invisible during play. No amount of runs would surface these.

Why the same god keeps coming back

Devotion encounters do not roll randomly. Both of the gods they offer are drawn from the gods you already hold, and the random fallback only runs if you are holding nothing at all.

A keepsake with charges left can override the first of the two outright, as long as that god is already in your run.

source RewardLogic.SetupRoomReward, GetInteractedGodThisRun

The moment your run stops being open

A run allows four Olympians. Take a boon from a fourth, and the Exit pool freezes to the four you have. Every other Olympian becomes impossible for the rest of the run, and so does every duo that needed one.

Hermes, Chaos, Selene, and the gods who interrupt you in encounter rooms are all outside that count and cost you nothing. Bounty runs lower the cap to one or two.

source HeroData.MaxGodsPerRun, ReachedMaxGods filtering LootTypeHistory on GodLoot

Nothing is nudging the odds toward gods you already have

An ordinary Exit reward picks uniformly from whatever is eligible. There is no weighting, no history term, no rubber banding. An Olympian you hold is exactly as likely as one you do not.

The recurrence you feel is the two rules above, not a tilted pool. And below the cap, an unheld god never becomes less likely. It goes straight from fully possible to impossible.

source RewardLogic.ChooseLoot

Level 2

You might get there eventually

Findable, after a lot of runs and some suspicion.

Rarity is worth far more on some boons than others

Every boon carries its own scaling table, and the shapes are not alike. Two Zeus boons, the same rarity jump:

Heaven Strike runs 0.8 at Common to 2.0 at Heroic, so it multiplies by 2.5. Storm Ring runs 1.0 to 1.6, a multiplier of 1.6.

The same Pom, the same upgrade, and nearly twice the payoff on one of them. The scaling shape is the interesting number, not the base value.

source RarityLevels in TraitData_Zeus

There is usually more than one way into a duo

A duo needs one boon from each of two listed groups, not two specific boons. Those groups are often the god's whole core set, so several different boons open the same duo.

Which means when three of them are on offer, you can take the one that spends a slot you were not going to use, instead of the one that costs you your Cast.

source OneFromEachSet in TraitData.lua

Level 3

You will work this out yourself

And it is better if you do. Open these only if you would rather not wait.

The real cost of a boon is not its numbers

It is the slot. Attack, Special, Cast, Sprint and Magick each hold one boon for the whole run, and filling one closes every build that wanted something else there.

A weak boon in a slot you needed is more expensive than a strong one in a slot you did not.

Which of the two Exits actually matters

The god, not the boons behind it. By the time you are looking at three offers the expensive decision is already made, and one of your four Olympian slots is spent.

So is this going to be a wiki? No, and it was genuinely considered. Two reasons. It is a monumental job, and the wiki already exists, actively maintained by a lot of people, and does a decent job of it. For lore especially, there is no sense rebuilding something that works. What this is instead: do what the existing tools do, a bit better, close the gaps between them, and add the things none of them have. Mechanical explanation will creep in where it earns its place, tooltips, what a boon actually does, why a rule works the way it does. That is not the same as being an encyclopedia, and the encyclopedia is not the plan.

The name

Ἐνοδία

Enodia, eh·NOH·dee·uh. An epithet of Hecate meaning “she of the ways”, from en hodos, on the road. She was invoked at crossroads and on night roads, where travellers left offerings and asked her to see them safely on.

She kept the job. Headmistress Hecate is standing in the Crossroads you walk out of every single run, and in the Orphic hymns she and Melinoë are the only two goddesses given the same epithet, krokopeplos, saffron-cloaked. The name was in the game before it was on this page.

Also considered

You found the moon. Well done.

Μόρος  Moros
God of doom and inevitability, son of Nyx, and the only one of his siblings privy to the designs of his older sisters, the Fates. He is the one who hands Melinoë the Fated List of Minor Prophecies, which made him the closest fit of anything proposed. He lost on search: he shares a name with a character, so he would have spent forever behind wiki pages and romance guides.
Καιρός  Kairos
The critical moment, as against chronos, plain sequential time. A winged youth with one lock of hair on his forehead, catchable as he comes and never once he has passed, which is the dead-build verdict already written in Greek. He lost for the same reason: too many companies got there first.

Earlier casualties, with cause of death. Trioditis, Hecate of the three ways, killed by a Dutch bank that took the same word for the same reason in 1980. Adresteia, “inescapable”, an epithet of the Fates and also of Nemesis, who is in the game. Nous, the back half of Melinoë’s own name and the Greek for mind, lost to being an ordinary English word. Clew, Ariadne’s thread and the literal origin of “clue”, lost to looking like a typo.

What is coming

The roadmap

Written in order of what gets built first. Phase one is useful on its own. If nothing else ever ships, it still answers the question the tool exists for.

01

The Exit

Next up

The reason to open the tool at all. The Codex already tells you what a single duo needs. None of this is about a single duo.

  • Exit modeThe three boons in front of you, ranked against the build you are actually playing, one sentence each.
  • What just diedCommit your Cast and a dozen builds close at once. You hear about it the moment it happens. Nothing in game tells you to stop trying.
  • Every build still openNot one pinned boon. All of them, sorted by how close you are and what each still needs.
  • Resume briefingCome back after a week and get told what you hold, what it is built around, and what closed while you were gone.

02

Before the run

Planned

Setup, for the decisions you make at the Crossroads rather than at an Exit.

  • Build archetypesEach one anchored on a duo or legendary, not a rigid list of thirty boons you will never draw.
  • Arcana against the Grasp budgetOnly the cards that actually matter for the build. Everything else is yours.
  • Keepsake sequencingA build implies a swap order across regions, not one keepsake. Nobody else does this.
  • Hammer picks per aspectWhich of the forty seven upgrades this build actually wants.

03

Memory

Planned

The part that makes it yours. Every run you log makes the advice more personal.

  • Run journalWhat you held, what you cleared, at what Fear. Build cards written for you from runs you actually played.
  • Screenshot importPoint it at your victory screen and it reads the boons off the image. No mod, no typing.
  • Gap analysisThe gods, aspects and slots you never touch, measured from your own runs rather than a checkbox.
  • Surprise meA complete plan drawn from your blind spots. “You have run this aspect twice in ninety runs and never with Hera.”

04

Automation

Someday

Worth doing, not worth doing first. All of it is PC only, and the manual path has to exist regardless.

  • Live run trackingA mod feeds the tool your run as you play it. No tapping at all.
  • Sharing and votingBuilds worth keeping, ranked by the Fear they have actually cleared.

Wherever you see Dora, it is not built yet. In the tool she marks every unfinished feature and stops appearing next to it the day it ships. On this page that would be all fourteen of them, which is a lot of Dora, so the icons above say what each thing is instead and she just holds the hard hat.
